criterion: caller whose contract the diff changed but did not update or cover with a test
finding: A map held in a card or a table cell emits data-afkv2-element for node ids that engine._element_ids never reads, so `check` passes duplicate element ids, and no plan step owns the fix.
why: The engine's contract is that `ids` holds every item, component and map node id and that each id is unique, but the new attribute also fires for nested maps, D-40's reason that a map goes in the `maps` list does not hold because S2's round_document.py accepts `map` as a card body root, and 0005 lists engine.py only to register the ingest verb while its Acceptance requires a note on every map node.
fix: Get an orchestrator ruling: make engine._element_ids walk every map with registry.walk and register its nodes (widen 0004 Scope, or add an explicit bullet and Scope note to 0005), and add a test that refuses 2 maps in cards with one node id.
evidence: diagram_map.py:17 `f' data-afkv2-element="{escape(node["id"])}"'`; engine.py `_element_ids` reads nodes only in `for m, map_ in enumerate(doc.get("maps") or [])`; invariants.py `ids holds every item, component and map node id`; feat/afkv2-s2 round_document.py:27 `PICTURES = {"map", "graph", "table", "sequence", "run-strip", "freestyle"}` with :126 `body["type"] not in PICTURES`; D-40 `S2's page says a map goes in the maps list`; 0005 Scope `afkv2/engine/engine.py   # register the ingest verb`; PRD AC-035 `on every element: map node`. Own probe through engine.check_document and page.build: 2 cards each with body map node `n-1` pass, with element attrs ['i-1','n-1','i-2','n-1']; a card body map with node id `i-2` beside item `i-2` passes, with attrs ['i-1','i-2','i-2']; a top-level map and a card map that share `n-1` pass; a card body map with round 99 passes, while the same node in `maps` is refused; a note with target `n-1` on a card body map is refused: `'n-1' resolves to no element`. No test in test_diagram_components.py pins these cases (read and grep, pattern `def test_.*(card|cell|note|element|target)`). Limit of the harm today: runtime.js holds no reference to data-afkv2-element (grep), so the duplicates have no reader until the 0005 notes work; the 0005 behaviour itself is not verified because that slice is not built.

criterion: Acceptance: A graph draws nodes and arrows, including grouped boxes for module structure (PRD CMP-5)
finding: An arrow that skips a rank is not visible: on edges a->c, c->b, a->b the a->b arrow runs behind box c and on top of the other two arrows, so the picture shows only a->c->b.
why: The acceptance bullet requires the graph to draw its arrows, and this common graph shape (a dependency that skips a step) draws a picture with one arrow missing, in the map as well because the map uses the same drawing; D-39 calls this a known gap, but D-39 is the slice's own record and is not a ruling on the bullet.
fix: Route a forward arrow that spans ranks around the boxes between its ends (for example, bend it past the stack and keep its label clear of other arrows), and add a test with a skip edge that asserts the path does not cross a box between its ends.
evidence: Separate probe with registry.render_component, nodes a,c,b, direction right. Boxes: a left 24, c left 264, b left 504, all top 24, width 176, height 36. Paths: 'a c' M200 42 C228 42 228 42 256 42; 'c b' M440 42 C468 42 468 42 496 42; 'a b' M200 42 C348 42 348 42 496 42. Label 'skip' at left 232, top 42, which is on the a->c arrow. Direction down gives the same result along x=112. diagram.css:15 '.afkv2-edges { ... z-index: 1' and diagram.css:25 box 'z-index: 2' with an opaque background. A grep of test_diagram_components.py for skip|behind|triangle|spans has 0 hits. D-39: 'An arrow that spans ranks or a back arrow can pass behind a box, and its label can sit on a box in a stack (known gap)'. Coordinates are observed; the page was not opened in a browser (visual result unverified).

criterion: Boundary values: edge labels placed with no collision check
finding: Edge labels of one source land on each other, and the opaque later label hides the text of the earlier one.
why: Headless Edge shows 3 failing inputs: edges a->b 'read' and a->b 'write' get the same left and top, so 'read' is fully hidden; direction down with a->b 'reads the order table' and a->c 'writes the audit row' sit 98px apart (shown as 'reads the order tal writes the audit row'); direction right with 2 stacked targets sit 28px apart, so a 2-line label is cut. This breaks PRD AC-042 'no content is hidden or cut off', and D-39 records only an arrow behind a box and a label on a box, not a label on a label.
fix: Give each edge label its own slot: separate parallel edges and fan-out labels along the cross axis, or widen the gap and stack spacing to the label size, and add a test that no 2 labels overlap.
evidence: label_main = from_main + min(layout.gap, run) // 2 / label_cross = from_cross + (tip_cross - from_cross) * (label_main - from_main) // run; .afkv2-edge-label { background: var(--bg); ... }

criterion: Boundary values: long edge label in direction right
finding: In direction right, a long edge label on the top row runs above the canvas, and the top lines cannot be reached by scrolling.
why: The gap is capped at NODE_WIDTH and no size grows for label height, unlike direction down at line 102. Headless Edge with a 170-character label between 2 single-line boxes showed the first line cut at the top of the scroll area; a label's top edge is above 0 once its height exceeds twice the row centre (84px, about 6 lines), and scrolling does not reach content above the origin. This breaks PRD AC-042 'no content is hidden or cut off'. A longer label loses more lines (inferred from the arithmetic, measured only at 170 characters).
fix: Add the tallest edge-label height to the top of the cross axis in direction right, or clamp the label top at 0 and grow the canvas.
evidence: return min(max(RANK_GAP, longest * EDGE_CHAR + 3 * HEAD), NODE_WIDTH); .afkv2-edge-label { position: absolute; transform: translate(-50%, -50%); ... }

criterion: Contract ## Verification unit row: render snapshots
finding: The unit tier does not hold the render snapshots that the contract row says it proves; the only whole-output check compares 2 renders in one run.
why: The contract's unit row lists 'render snapshots' and PRD 'Page engine: deterministic tests (schema checks, render snapshots, ...)' names them, but no stored expected output exists, so a change in the markup that keeps the checked classes and words passes.
fix: Add one stored expected HTML per diagram type under the test fixtures and compare bytes, or get the row changed on the record if substring checks are the intended proof.
evidence: Contract: '| unit | `afk-python -m pytest afkv2/tests/engine/test_diagram_components.py -q` | render snapshots; prop refusals; diagram in a card and in a table cell; map colours |'. Test line 150: 'assert draw(name) == draw(name)'. A case-insensitive grep of the test file for snapshot|golden has 0 hits. A listing of afkv2/tests/engine/fixtures shows host-*.txt, v1-*.json, v0-sdd-pass.json and send_from_edge.mjs, with no diagram output.

finding: The styling test matches a class name as a substring, so a class with no rule passes when a longer class name starts with it.
why: `.afkv2-box` is found in `.afkv2-box-label`, so the bullet 'Each component owns its styling' is not proved for the base classes that hold most of the layout.
fix: Match the whole class name with a pattern such as `\.name(?![\w-])`.
evidence: `assert drawn and not [word for word in drawn if f".{word}" not in STYLES]`. Separate check: with all rules of the exact class removed from the text of diagram.css, the substring still matched for afkv2-box, afkv2-edge, afkv2-group, afkv2-seq, afkv2-seq-msg, afkv2-diagram and afkv2-run-step.

finding: The escape test misses the group label and the 2 id attributes.
why: An author string reaches the page through a group label, a map node id and an edge end, and none of them is in the test input, so removing `escape` there passes and HTML from a document can reach the page.
fix: Add a group label, a node id and an edge end that hold `<` and `"` to the test input, and assert the escaped form for each.
evidence: Input sets only title, node label, edge label, step label and detail, actor label and message text. SURVIVED: `{escape(title)}` to `{title}`; `data-afkv2-edge` without escape; `data-afkv2-element="{node["id"]}"`. Not verified: whether a real document can hold such an id, because TEXT sets only minLength.

finding: BAD_PROPS has no off-boundary or wrong-type row for many schema rules.
why: The bullet 'refuses bad props naming the item and the field' is unproved for these rules: `round` 0 is the boundary of `minimum: 1`, and the test on round covers only the upper end, at line 294.
fix: Add rows: round 0, round as a string, empty id and empty label, non-string title, edge label and step detail, `actors: []`, an extra field on an actor, message, step and group, and a message and an edge without `from` and `to`.
evidence: SURVIVED: `"round": {"type": "integer"}`; `"round": {}`; TEXT without minLength; `TITLE = {}`; edge label `{}`; detail `{}`; actors without minItems; no additionalProperties on actor, message, step and group; message `required` only `text`; edge `required: []`.

finding: No test reads the path of an arrow: the arrow assert only echoes the from and to ids of the input.
why: A graph that draws no arrow line, no arrowhead, or an arrow in the wrong direction passes all 97 tests, so the bullet 'A graph draws nodes and arrows' has no proof for the arrows.
fix: Parse the `d` of each path and assert that a forward arrow starts on the edge of the source box and ends at the edge of the target box, in both directions, and that a back arrow ends at its target. Assert that each arrowhead has a non-empty `d`.
evidence: `assert arrows(html) == ["g-controller g-service", "g-service g-store"]`, and EDGE_PATH captures only `data-afkv2-edge`, which diagram_boxes.py writes from edge["from"] and edge["to"]. In-memory source mutants of diagram_boxes.py that SURVIVED: `_arrows` swaps from and to places; `_forward` returns empty curve and tip; `_backward` returns empty curve and tip; arrowhead `d=""`. A no-op control mutant survived and other mutants were killed, so the method works. mutation-probe.sh not run: this slice has no production Java. A separate probe of the unmutated code showed correct end points, so this is a test gap and not a shown bug.

finding: The group frame assert runs only in direction `right`, with short group labels.
why: The `down` frame has its own rect expression and its own `head_room`, and a long group label has its own head height, but no test reads a frame in those cases, so a wrong frame there passes.
fix: Parametrize the group test on direction, and add a long group label. Assert that each member is inside its frame, below the frame label, and that the frame stays on the canvas.
evidence: GRAPH has `"direction": "right"`; test_boxes_never_overlap_and_fit_the_canvas uses `down` and long group labels but reads only boxes. SURVIVED: `else (cross, low - FRAME - heads[group], ...)` to `else (cross, low, 1, 1)`; `head_room = 0`; head height fixed at `GROUP_LINE + FRAME`. The `right` frame mutant was killed at line 333.

finding: No test asserts the box and gap sizes that come from the label: the layout tests check only that boxes do not overlap.
why: D-39 rests on 'an estimated label size', but a fixed size is also free of overlap, so a box that ignores its label, a map that loses its head room, and a held component in a small box all pass.
fix: Assert that a longer label gives a taller box, that a map box is taller than a graph box with the same label by the head height, that a held component gets the held size, that a longer edge label gives a larger gap, and that the edge label position and max-width follow the arrow.
evidence: SURVIVED in diagram_boxes.py and diagram_map.py: height `BOX_PADDING + head + LINE`; `return NODE_WIDTH, BOX_PADDING + head + LINE` for a held label; `draw_boxes(props, 0, _node_parts)`; `_gap` returns RANK_GAP in both directions; forward label at (0, 0); no `max-width`.

finding: No test asserts rank order when a node has 2 incoming paths of different length.
why: `_ranks` takes the longest path, but the only multi-parent fixture asserts boxes and overlap, so a rank that ignores the longest path and puts a target beside its source passes.
fix: Add a case with edges p->t, r1->r2, r2->t and node order p, r1, r2, t, and assert that each non-back arrow runs forward along the ranks (t after r2).
evidence: Mutant `ranks[target] = max(ranks[target], ranks[node] + 1)` to `ranks[target] = ranks[node] + 1` SURVIVED. Read, not run: on that case the mutant gives t rank 1 after r2 gave it rank 2.

finding: The sequence tests do not prove that an actor stands in the column of its messages.
why: Actor column, lifeline column, lifeline length and the grid column count are not asserted, so a diagram with all actors in column 1 passes, and the bullet 'draws actors and ordered messages' is proved only for the messages.
fix: Assert `grid-column` of each actor and lifeline against the order of the actors, the lifeline `grid-row` end against the message count, the `repeat(N,` count, and the grid column of a self message.
evidence: `assert all(actor["label"] in html for actor in SEQUENCE["actors"])` and `assert html.count(SEQ_LIFE) == 3`. SURVIVED in diagram_sequence.py: `_actor(1, actor)`; lifeline `grid-column:1`; lifeline `grid-row:2 / 3`; `repeat(1,`; `margin = ""`.

criterion: Boundary values: back-arrow label in direction down
finding: In direction down, a back-arrow label wraps in a column of about 38px, one or two words per line.
why: The label's left is far - BACK_ARC // 4, which is 38px from the canvas right edge when the arrow is on the last band, and an absolute element with auto width shrinks to the space left of it. Headless Edge with b->a 'retry after the time-out' drew 5 lines ('retry / after / the / time- / out'); the same label in direction right drew 1 line. The text stays readable but breaks mid-word.
fix: Reserve room for the label width to the right of a band that holds a back arrow in direction down, or set an explicit label width.
evidence: label = layout.label_left_top((from_main + tip_main) // 2, far - BACK_ARC // 4); cross_end = cross - BAND_GAP + START

finding: The 'own module' test does not link the registry entry to the module.
why: The file check and the lookup are independent, so the test still passes if one module registers all 4 types and the others only exist.
fix: Assert `kind.render.__module__ == f"page_component_{Path(module).stem}"`, the module name that registry.load_components gives.
evidence: `assert (ENGINE_DIR / "components" / module).is_file()` and `assert kind.name == name and ...`. Found by reading; not run as a mutant.

finding: Possible conditional test logic: an if/elif/else on the type name builds the input inside the escape test.
why: The checklist asks to split or parameterize a branch in a test body; here the branch hides which fields each type covers, which is how the gaps in the escape input stay hard to see.
fix: Move each type's bad input into a parameter table with the expected escaped strings.
evidence: `if name == "run-strip":` ... `elif name == "sequence":` ... `else:`; the same form is at line 343: `if node["group"] is None:`.
